y-m-40-07.title: Two ways to count when choosing 5 fruits
y-m-40-07.topic: Combinations with repeats: choices wey no different and choices wey different
y-m-40-07.goal: Show say even if you start with same numbers 5 and 3, answer fit be 21 or 243 based on wetin different; check relation (30) between both values and explain difference to friend.
y-m-40-07.material: Fruit shop get plenty apples, pears, tangerines. Fruits of same kind no different from each other. You wan buy 5 fruits. Two people give different answers. Yunsu: ‘3×3×3×3×3=3⁵=243 ways.’ Hana: ‘Na decide how many of each kind to buy, so 7C2=21 ways.’ Think which answer correct when situation change.
y-m-40-07.thinking.0: Tell apart say both models answer different situations
y-m-40-07.thinking.1: Work out how many times one value enter the other
y-m-40-07.thinking.2: Explain difference to friend by separating situations
y-m-40-07.prereq.1: Know n!, ways to arrange different things in a row, and product rule. For this task, first time you use arrangement count for identical items (5!÷(2!×2!)).
y-m-40-07.s.s1.prompt: For situation above (buy 5 fruits, same-kind fruit no different), which answer fit?
y-m-40-07.s.s1.hint.0: Start with small case (2 fruits), directly list every group with a apples, b pears, c tangerines where a+b+c=5.
y-m-40-07.s.s1.hint.1: Use (2 apples, 2 pears, 1 tangerine) as example, check whether formula wey decide kind of each of 5 count same selection more than once.
y-m-40-07.s.s1.o.a: 243 ways. Because you decide kind for each of the 5
y-m-40-07.s.s1.r.a: Na thinking wey count as if di 5 fruits different from each other. Check whether e match condition say same-kind fruit no different.
y-m-40-07.s.s1.o.b: 10 ways. See am as choosing 3 out of 5 (5C3)
y-m-40-07.s.s1.r.b: Na thinking wey misunderstand deciding fruit kinds as ‘choose how many out of 5.’
y-m-40-07.s.s1.o.c: Cannot decide. You need know how many of each fruit shop get
y-m-40-07.s.s1.r.c: Na thinking wey no use condition ‘plenty dey’ and treat information as not enough.
y-m-40-07.s.s1.o.d: 21 ways. Only consider how many apples, pears, tangerines dem buy
y-m-40-07.s.s1.r.d: Na thinking wey notice say only count of each kind matter, because same-kind fruit no different.
y-m-40-07.s.s1.explain: Since same-kind fruits no different, only (apple count, pear count, tangerine count) change. These are nonnegative integer triples wey sum to 5. Answer na 7C2=21: choose 2 divider positions among 7 slots when you line up 5 ○'s and 2 dividers. Listing (5,0,0), (4,1,0), … directly also give 21.
y-m-40-07.s.s2.prompt: New situation. 5 friends (all different people) each choose one apple, pear, or tangerine. You record who choose what too. Which answer fit this situation?
y-m-40-07.s.s2.hint.0: First write number of records if 1 friend dey and if 2 friends dey.
y-m-40-07.s.s2.hint.1: Compare how dis differ from previous situation in whether people different and whether same-kind fruit different.
y-m-40-07.s.s2.o.a: 243 ways. Each of 5 people choose one of 3
y-m-40-07.s.s2.r.a: Na thinking wey multiply each person's independent choices because people different from each other.
y-m-40-07.s.s2.o.b: 21 ways. Same fruits no different, so answer same as before
y-m-40-07.s.s2.r.b: Na thinking wey use earlier situation answer even though people different and you record who choose.
y-m-40-07.s.s2.o.c: 15 ways. Pair up 5 people in twos then share dem among 3
y-m-40-07.s.s2.r.c: Na thinking wey mistake am as pairing up 5 people. First check what each person choose.
y-m-40-07.s.s2.explain: People different and you record who choose what, so each person's choice get 3 options regardless of others. 3×3×3×3×3=243 ways. Before, people buy fruits and same-kind fruits no different, so answer 21 ways.
y-m-40-07.s.s3.prompt: In earlier situation, buying ‘2 apples, 2 pears, 1 tangerine’ na one of 21 ways. In new situation (survey of 5 people), how many records show ‘2 people choose apple, 2 choose pear, 1 choose tangerine’ ?
y-m-40-07.s.s3.hint.0: First count ways to choose 2 apple-choosing people from 5, then count ways to choose 2 pear-choosing people from di rest.
y-m-40-07.s.s3.hint.1: Name people 가, 나, 다, 라, 마; write ‘가 and 나 apple, 다 and 라 pear, 마 tangerine’ as one record, then write few more.
y-m-40-07.s.s3.r.a: Na value wey only count who di one person wey choose tangerine be. Think how to split people wey choose apple and pear too.
y-m-40-07.s.s3.r.b: Na thinking wey count without overlap ways to split 5 people into 2 apples, 2 pears, 1 tangerine.
y-m-40-07.s.s3.r.c: Na value from choosing in order who get apple, pear, tangerine and count 5!÷2. You need divide one more time for repeats within same kind.
y-m-40-07.s.s3.r.d: Na value wey only count ways to choose 2 apple people (5C2). Remaining 3 people still fit split between pears and tangerines in more ways.
y-m-40-07.s.s3.explain: Ways to choose 2 apple people from 5 na 5C2=10. Ways to choose 2 pear people among remaining 3 na 3C2=3, and last person choose tangerine; so 10×3=30 ways (5!÷(2!×2!)=30 too). Add records for each of 21 combinations, total na 243. For example, (5, 0, 0) gives 1 way, and (2, 2, 1) gives 30 ways.
y-m-40-07.s.s4.prompt: Hana and Yunsu answers different no be because one wrong, but because dem count different things. Explain what situations each answer, 21 and 243, fit answer so your friend understand.
y-m-40-07.s.s4.hint.0: Write one line each on ‘wetin different’ for both situations, then compare.
y-m-40-07.s.s4.hint.1: Choose one everyday scene for each (fruit shop, survey).
y-m-40-07.s.s4.selfAssess.0: For situation where answer na 21, I write wetin no different?
y-m-40-07.s.s4.selfAssess.1: For situation where answer na 243, I write wetin different?
y-m-40-07.s.s4.selfAssess.2: I use everyday examples wey help friend tell both situations apart?
y-m-40-07.s.s4.model.0: Yunsu 243 answers situation where you record wetin each of 5 people choose, including who choose am. Hana 21 answers situation where same-kind fruits no different and you only count how many of each kind dem buy.
y-m-40-07.s.s4.model.1: If you buy 5 fruits and put dem in basket, only number of apples, pears, tangerines change, so 21 ways. But if you record each person's choice, even same count combination get different records, so 243 ways.

y-m-40-05.title: Dividing 6 books into two bundles [6]
y-m-40-05.topic: Combinations: division depends on whether bundles are distinguished.
y-m-40-05.goal: Know say same sentence fit give 2 different answers, talk wetin more information problem need to decide answer, then count for new situation where dem set that information.
y-m-40-05.material: 6 different books dey. You wan divide dem into 2 bundles with 3 books each. Order or position of books inside bundle no matter. How many ways dey? Jieun say 6C3=20 ways; Hyeonu say 20÷2=10 ways.
y-m-40-05.thinking.0: Judge whether information for problem enough
y-m-40-05.thinking.1: Say yourself which information you need and turn am to condition sentence
y-m-40-05.thinking.2: Connect case where bundles different with case where dem no be different
y-m-40-05.prereq.1: Know meaning of combination nCr. Know idea of dividing by number of times dem count same division when e repeat.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.prompt: Which judgment fit Jieun and Hyeonu answers best?
y-m-40-05.s.s1.hint.0: Write one line each about wetin Jieun and Hyeonu calculations count as ‘different things.’
y-m-40-05.s.s1.hint.1: Use small case with 4 books (a, b, c, d) in 2 bundles of 2: list all ways direct and compare with answers from both formulas.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.o.a: 20 ways correct. Once you choose 3 books for first bundle, di rest don decide.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.r.a: Na calculation for when you treat di 2 bundles as different. E no check whether problem talk so.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.o.b: 10 ways correct. Swapping di 2 bundles still be same division.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.r.b: Na calculation for when bundles no different. E no check whether problem talk so.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.o.c: E fit be 20 or 10 ways, based on whether di 2 bundles different.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.r.c: Na thinking wey notice say one condition wey sentence no state (whether bundles different) split di answer.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.o.d: You need book price and page number to decide either answer
y-m-40-05.s.s1.r.d: Book features no relate to number of ways. Look again which condition split answer.
y-m-40-05.s.s1.explain: Answer depend on whether di 2 bundles get labels (for example, whether you don decide who go receive each one). If dem get labels, choosing 3 books for first bundle decide di rest, so 20 ways. If no labels, {a, b, c} and {d, e, f} na same division as {d, e, f} and {a, b, c}, so 10 ways. Di problem sentence alone no decide which one.
y-m-40-05.s.s2.prompt: Make and write one situation where answer na 20 ways and one where na 10 ways, each at least one sentence. Make clear wetin different between dem.
y-m-40-05.s.s2.hint.0: Turn sentence patterns behind Jieun and Hyeonu answers into everyday examples (boxes, people, teams).
y-m-40-05.s.s2.hint.1: For sentences you make, check whether swapping 2 bundles make different division or same one.
y-m-40-05.s.s2.placeholder: Example: Case wey give 20 ways na ...
y-m-40-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Difference between both situations show as ‘whether bundles different’?
y-m-40-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: For 20-way situation, dem don decide who receive which bundle?
y-m-40-05.s.s2.selfAssess.2: For 10-way situation, na same division if you swap di 2 bundles?
y-m-40-05.s.s2.model.0: If you give 3 books each to 2 people A and B, e clear who get which bundle, so 20 ways. If you put books into 2 identical boxes and boxes no different, na 10 ways.
y-m-40-05.s.s2.model.1: 20 ways: divide 3 books each into ‘bundle to read today’ and ‘bundle to read tomorrow’ (each get different use). 10 ways: just divide into two piles of 3 without names; swapping piles still same division.
y-m-40-05.s.s3.prompt: You wan divide 6 different books into 3 bundles of 2. Dis time bundles no get labels and no different from each other. How many ways dey?
y-m-40-05.s.s3.hint.0: Assume say you put labels 1, 2, 3 on bundles and count first.
y-m-40-05.s.s3.hint.1: Count how many ways you fit write bundles {a, b}, {c, d}, {e, f} by only changing their order.
y-m-40-05.s.s3.r.a: Na answer if di 3 bundles get labels (6C2×4C2×2C2). Without labels, dem count same division more than once.
y-m-40-05.s.s3.r.b: Na thinking wey count with labels first, then see say when labels removed, dem repeat same division as many times as bundle orders.
y-m-40-05.s.s3.r.c: Na labeled answer divided only by 2. Count again how many times e repeat when labels removed.
y-m-40-05.s.s3.r.d: Na labeled answer divided only by 3. Count how many ways to line up 3 bundles.
y-m-40-05.s.s3.explain: If 3 bundles get labels (1, 2, 3), answer na 6C2×4C2×2C2=15×6×1=90 ways. Without labels, dem count same division 3!=6 times, number of bundle orders, so 90÷6=15 ways. Listing and counting all 6 books also give 15 ways.

y-m-40-03.title: Compare ways people stand so they are not beside each other
y-m-40-03.topic: Permutations: comparing arrangements with people nonadjacent
y-m-40-03.goal: Find two methods giving same value 480, fix error in one, test which extends with added conditions. [480]
y-m-40-03.material: Six people A-F stand in line for photo, 6 spots. Adjacent means next spot. How many arrangements have A and B nonadjacent? Four friends explain methods and answers differ. [6]
y-m-40-03.prereq.1: Know n! arrangements of n distinct people and permutation nPr.
y-m-40-03.s.s1.hint.0: Put four answers side by side; first select those with differing values.
y-m-40-03.s.s1.hint.1: For solutions with different values, check small cases (A first, A middle) whether each line choice count works always.
y-m-40-03.s.s1.o.a: Seoyun: from 720 total subtract 5!=120 arrangements with A,B as a bundle, giving 600. [720 5 120 600]
y-m-40-03.s.s1.r.a: This subtracts only bundle arrangements and misses 2 internal orders of A,B.
y-m-40-03.s.s1.o.b: Jia: subtract adjacent bundle cases, 5!×2 internal orders, from 720, giving 480. [720 5 2 480]
y-m-40-03.s.s1.r.b: This counts adjacent cases as bundle × internal order, then subtracts from total.
y-m-40-03.s.s1.o.c: Hajun: place A (6 ways), B in 4 spots, arrange other 4: 6×4×4!=576. [6 4 4 6 4 4 576]
y-m-40-03.s.s1.r.c: This assumes B always has 4 spots wherever A stands. [4]
y-m-40-03.s.s1.o.d: Doyun: arrange C,D,E,F (4!), insert A and B in order into two of 5 gaps: 4!×5×4=480. [4 5 4 5 4 480]
y-m-40-03.s.s1.r.d: This puts nonadjacent people in gaps later, blocking adjacency from start.
y-m-40-03.s.s1.explain: Jia and Doyun get 480 (720−240=480; 24×20=480). Seoyun missed 2 internal A/B orders, counting adjacent as 120 instead of 240. For Hajun, A at either end gives B 4 spots, but A in one of 4 middle spots gives only 3; he counted 4 always. Check both result and each line assumption. [480 720 240 480 24 20 480 2 120 240 4 4 3 4]
y-m-40-03.s.s2.prompt: Explain error in Hajun 576 and fix to get 480. [576 480]
y-m-40-03.s.s2.hint.0: Mark spots B cannot use when A first and when A third.
y-m-40-03.s.s2.hint.1: Table number of B spots for each A position; add them.
y-m-40-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you separate A at either end from A in middle?
y-m-40-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you list available B spots separately for cases?
y-m-40-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you check corrected calculation gives 480? [480]
y-m-40-03.s.s2.model.0: A at either end has one neighbor spot, so B has 4 choices; A in one of four middle spots has 2 neighbor spots, leaving 3. Thus (2×4+4×3)×4!=20×24=480. [4 4 3 2 4 4 3 4 20 24 480]
y-m-40-03.s.s2.model.1: Hajun used 6×4 though B choices depend on A position. In middle, only 3 spots; replace 6×4 by 20, then multiply 24 ways for other four: 480. [4 6 4 4 3 6 4 20 24 4 480]
y-m-40-03.s.s3.prompt: Now six people, no two of A,B,C adjacent. Extend Doyun method (arrange others, insert into gaps): how many? [6]
y-m-40-03.s.s3.hint.0: Arrange D,E,F; name gaps without drawing: front, gap1, gap2, back. [1 2]
y-m-40-03.s.s3.hint.1: If two enter same gap, what happens? Then count placements in different gaps.
y-m-40-03.s.s3.r.a: This counts insertion only, without multiplying 3! arrangements of D,E,F. [3]
y-m-40-03.s.s3.r.b: This arranges D,E,F first, then places A,B,C into different gaps in order.
y-m-40-03.s.s3.r.c: Assumes A,B,C each choose any of 4 spots; misses same-gap placements make adjacent. [4]
y-m-40-03.s.s3.r.d: This just uses all 6! arrangements, ignoring nonadjacent condition. [6]
y-m-40-03.s.s3.explain: D,E,F line up 3!=6 ways. Four gaps total (two ends, two between). Choose three different gaps and assign A,B,C in order: 4×3×2=24. Total 6×24=144. Subtracting from total gets complex due three adjacent pairs and overlaps. [3 6 4 2 2 4 3 2 24 6 24 144]

y-m-40-04.thinking.1: Change your judgment with new information
y-m-40-04.prereq.0: H3 for dis batch na only difficulty tier for production task, no be school grade. E assume say from high school Common Mathematics counting unit, you don learn addition and product rules, and meaning and calculation of permutations nPr and combinations nCr (read nPr as ‘n P r’ and nCr as ‘n C r’).
y-m-40-04.title: Round table and bracelet: rule for treating arrangements as same
y-m-40-04.topic: Circular and necklace permutations: how sameness rule changes count
y-m-40-04.goal: For circular arrangements, track count as rule for sameness changes and check formula range.
y-m-40-04.material: Place 6 distinct people or beads in circle. Circle has no front, so rotations count same. Information comes stepwise; update judgment each time. [6]
y-m-40-04.thinking.2: Test formula range using small cases
y-m-40-04.prereq.1: Know n! line arrangements and division by repeat-count; no need circular permutation formula.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.prompt: Read each new fact and continue judgment.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.hint.0: Each step write sameness rule in one line.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.hint.1: With 3 people/beads, list arrangements and group by rule. [3 3]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.info: Six people sit round table, unnumbered chairs; rotations count same. Mina says 6!=720 like line. [6 6 720]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.after: Six rotations of one arrangement all same, so 720 counts each 6 times: 720÷6=120. Fix one person (Mina) and arrange other 5: 5!=120 too. [6 720 6 720 6 120 5 5 120]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.o.a: 720 correct; same as arranging 6 people in order. [720 6]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This ignores rotation-sameness and treats it like a line.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: More than 720. Circle has two directions, so more. [720]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This thinks circle increases count; sameness rules reduce count.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Less than 720. Rotated duplicates counted several times. [720]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This recognizes repetition caused by sameness rule.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.1.info: Now make bracelet from 6 distinct beads. Rotations and flips (clockwise/counterclockwise swap) count same. Does earlier 120 still hold? [6 120]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.1.after: All beads distinct, flipping cannot match original by rotation alone because neighbor order reverses. Thus 120 arrangements pair into bracelets: 120÷2=60. [6 120 120 2 60]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This increases count even though sameness rule expanded.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Still 120. We only merged rotations, nothing changes. [120]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This ignores new rule merging flipped bracelets.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.1.o.c: 60 ways. Two arrangements overlapping by flip merge. [60]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: This sees pairs merge under added rule.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.info: Use formula (n−1)!÷2 for n-bead bracelet? Make distinct 3-bead and 2-bead bracelets directly and compare formula. [1 2 3 2]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.after: Three-bead bracelet ABC and ACB become same on flip, so 1 way ((3−1)!÷2=1). Two beads have 1 arrangement, but formula gives 0.5; use formula only n≥3. [1 3 1 2 1 2 1 0.5 3]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Formula right for any n, so n=2 gives 0.5 ways. [2 0.5]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This trusts formula without checking that count cannot be 0.5. [0.5]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: For n=3 formula matches 1. For n=2 it is not integer, so count separately. [3 1 2]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This decides formula range by direct small cases.
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.o.c: For n=3, (3−1)!=2 ways in reality, so formula wrong even there. [3 3 1 2 3]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: This misses 3-bead bracelet merges when flipped. [3]
y-m-40-04.s.s1.reflect: Each new fact changed not calculation method but what counts same. Each added sameness rule changes repeat count and formula. Testing small cases reveals formula range.
y-m-40-04.s.s2.prompt: People at table and 6-bead bracelet both place same 6 things in circle, yet counts differ (120 vs 60). Explain based on people/beads. [6 6 6 120 60]
y-m-40-04.s.s2.hint.0: Imagine flip bracelet and use 3 beads to show how neighbor order changes. [3]
y-m-40-04.s.s2.hint.1: With 3 people sitting, could swapping left and right neighbors count as same? [3]
y-m-40-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you say people and bracelets differ on whether flipping counts same?
y-m-40-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Is this difference why count halves?
y-m-40-04.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you explain why flip does not count same for seated people?
y-m-40-04.s.s2.model.0: People cannot be flipped while seated, so mirror image is different: 120 ways. Flipped bracelet pairs arrangements into same shape, halving 120 to 60. [120 120 60]
y-m-40-04.s.s2.model.1: When bracelet flips, clockwise and counterclockwise orders merge, giving 60. For seats, swapping left/right neighbors makes a different situation, so they stay distinct. [60]

y-m-40-08.title: If construction block road, how many routes disappear?
y-m-40-08.topic: Grid routes: number of shortest routes when sections block
y-m-40-08.goal: After finding number of shortest routes, judge step by step how blocking one section change am; understand say with 2 blocked sections, remove routes wey overlap only once.
y-m-40-08.material: Town roads form checkerboard. For rectangular grid 4 units wide and 3 tall, move from home (lower-left corner) to school (upper-right), only right (→) or up (↑), one unit each move. Write junction as (horizontal position, vertical position); home na (0, 0), school na (4, 3). Information go come step by step.
y-m-40-08.thinking.0: Adjust counted value based on new condition
y-m-40-08.thinking.1: Compare which section get biggest effect
y-m-40-08.prereq.1: Know number of orders to arrange moves (combination nCr) when right/up move counts fixed. Know how to write junction position as ordered pair (horizontal position, vertical position).
y-m-40-08.s.s1.hint.0: For each step, first write in one line which ‘routes wey you no fit use now’.
y-m-40-08.s.s1.hint.1: Count separately routes to junction before blocked section and routes from junction after am to school.
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.0.info: All roads open. Any route home-school get → 4 times and ↑ 3 times.
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.0.ask: How many different shortest routes dey from home to school?
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.0.after: Choose positions for 3 ↑ among 7 moves; rest na →. That gives 7C3=35 ways. Choosing positions for 4 → also gives 7C4=35.
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Na value wey count 7 moves as number of routes.
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Na product of horizontal units and vertical units (like number of squares in rectangle).
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This decides places where 3 upward moves occur among 7 moves. [3 7]
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.0.r.d: This chooses locations for 3 of 7, but also treats order as different. [3 7]
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.1.info: Road section between (2,1) and (3,1) (one right move) under construction, cannot pass. Other sections open. [2 1 3 1]
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.1.after: To pass that section, 3 ways from (0,0) to (2,1), and 3 ways from (3,1) to (4,3). The 3×3=9 routes are lost; 35−9=26. [3 0 0 2 1 3 3 1 4 3 3 3 9 35 9 26]
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Still 35 ways. Some paths avoid that section, so count unchanged. [35]
y-m-40-08.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This misses routes through blocked section disappear.

y-m-40-02.title: Finding numbers with 12 divisors [12]
y-m-40-02.topic: Counting divisors with product rule (using prime factorization)
y-m-40-02.goal: Few examples alone no prove divisor-count rule from prime exponents. Explain why rule works and make several numbers meeting a condition.
y-m-40-02.material: Minseo claim about divisor count of natural N: 12 divisors are 1,2,3,4,6,12 (6 total); 18: 1,2,3,6,9,18 (6); 20: 1,2,4,5,10,20 (6). Since 12=2²×3, 18=2×3², 20=2²×5, divisor count equals product of each prime exponent plus 1. Test rule, then make numbers meeting a condition. [12 1 2 3 4 6 12 6 18 1 2 3 6 9 18 6 20 1 2 4 5 10 20 6 12 2 3 18 2 3 20 2 5 1]
y-m-40-02.thinking.0: Check how varied examples behind generalization are

y-m-40-02.s.s1.o.a: Yes. It matched rule all three times, so generally true.
y-m-40-02.s.s1.r.a: This assumes many examples allow generalization; it did not check whether examples have varied forms.
y-m-40-02.s.s1.o.b: No. All three numbers have same exponent pattern; other patterns not tested.
y-m-40-02.s.s1.r.b: This judgment checks diversity of example forms, not count.
y-m-40-02.s.s1.o.c: No. These are the only numbers with 6 divisors, so no rule. [6]
y-m-40-02.s.s1.r.c: Other numbers have 6 divisors too, e.g. 28 and 32. That does not decide whether rule is right. [6 28 32]
y-m-40-02.s.s1.o.d: Yes. Their prime factors are mixed differently, enough.
y-m-40-02.s.s1.r.d: Different prime-factor mixes are not same as different exponent patterns. Compare patterns.
y-m-40-02.s.s1.explain: All three have exponent pattern (2,1): 12=2²×3, 18=2¹×3², 20=2²×5. Not yet tested: one exponent only or three primes. 16=2⁴ has 5 divisors 1,2,4,8,16; rule gives 4+1=5. 60=2²×3×5 gives (2+1)(1+1)(1+1)=12. Both fit, but still examples. Next explain rule from divisor structure. [2 1 12 2 3 18 2 3 20 2 5 16 2 5 1 2 4 8 16 4 1 5 60 2 3 5 2 1 1 1 1 1 12]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.prompt: Assume Minseo rule correct. Make 3 distinct N=2^a×3^b with exactly 12 divisors and N≤200. a and b are nonnegative integer exponents. [3 2 3 12 200 2 3 0]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.hint.1: For each pair find a,b, calculate 2^a×3^b and check N≤200. [2 3 200]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.ok.c1: a and b are nonnegative integers. [0]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.fail.c1: Choose nonnegative integer exponents a and b. [0]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.fail.c2: Divisor count no be 12. Recalculate using rule. [12]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.prompt: Using divisors of 12=2²×3, explain why N=2^a×3^b has (a+1)×(b+1) divisors. [12 2 3 2 3 1 1]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.hint.0: List divisors of 12; table how many factors 2 and 3 multiply in each. [12 2 3]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.hint.1: List possible powers of 2 and count pairs with powers of 3. [2 3]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Your divisors split into power-of-2 and power-of-3 parts? [2 3]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: Did you say 0th power counts too, so number is exponent plus 1? [0 1]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: Did you count by pairing choices for the two parts?
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.model.0: Divisors of 12 have form 2^i×3^j; i has 3 choices 0,1,2; j has 2 choices 0,1. Pairing gives 3×2=6. Generally i=0..a has a+1 choices; j has b+1, giving (a+1)(b+1). [12 2 3 3 0 1 2 2 0 1 3 2 6 0 1 1 1 1]
y-m-40-02.s.s2.because.model.1: Divisors of 12=2²×3 are 1,2,4,3,6,12. Choose 2-part from 1,2,4 (0th to 2nd power, 2+1 choices), 3-part from 1,3; multiply to make one divisor. Thus 3×2 ways. [12 2 3 1 2 4 3 6 12 2 1 2 4 0 2 2 1 3 1 3 3 2]
y-m-40-02.s.s3.prompt: Among natural numbers ≤200, are above numbers (72,96,108) only ones with 12 divisors? [200 72 96 108 12]
y-m-40-02.s.s3.hint.0: Try exponent triples (a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=12 and check use of primes besides 2 and 3. [1 1 1 12 12 2 3]
y-m-40-02.s.s3.hint.1: List all divisors of a candidate like 2²×3×5 and count whether 12. [2 3 5 12]
y-m-40-02.s.s3.o.a: No. Some use prime 5 too, e.g. 60. [5 60]
y-m-40-02.s.s3.r.a: This tests “only these?” with one counterexample using a new prime.
y-m-40-02.s.s3.o.b: Cannot tell. Too many numbers with 12 divisors; need count up to 200. [12 200]
y-m-40-02.s.s3.r.b: Check whether one counterexample answers this without counting all.
y-m-40-02.s.s3.o.c: Yes. Numbers with 12 divisors only form 2^a×3^b. [12 2 3]
y-m-40-02.s.s3.r.c: This assumes only primes 2 and 3. Test numbers using primes 5 or 7. [2 3 5 7]

y-m-40-01.material: Five cards get digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, one digit each. Choose 3 different cards and line dem up to make three-digit number. But if 2 or 4 dey ones place, dem don already use that card, so hundreds place get only 3 choices after leaving out 0. When number of later choices change based on earlier choice, you no fit simply multiply choice counts. Line 1 and line 3 correct for every case; line 4 calculation use value from line 2. y-m-40-01.s.s2.r.c: Na method wey separate ones=0 from ones=2 or 4, then separately count possibilities using remaining cards for each case.
y-m-40-01.s.s2.r.d: Na value wey count only case ones place na 2 or 4 (2×3×3), leaving out case ones place na 0.
y-m-40-01.s.s2.explain: If ones place na 0, hundreds and tens use remaining 4 cards, so 4×3=12 numbers. If ones place na 2 or 4 (2 choices), hundreds get 3 choices (leave out 0 and card already used), and tens get 3 choices, so 2×3×3=18 numbers. 12+18=30. Another method: remove odd numbers (ones place 1 or 3: 2×3×3=18) from all three-digit numbers, 4×4×3=48; you also get 30.

y-m-40-01.s.s3.o.b: Correct. Three even cards fit go ones place, so 3×4×3=36 3

y-m-40-01.s.s3.explain: If no 0 card, whether ones digit 2 or 4, all 4 remaining cards fit hundreds place; then 3 cards remain for tens. So 2×4×3=24 correct (listing also gives 24). Multiplication method okay; check whether later choice count depend on earlier choice. [0 2 4 4 3 2 4 3 24 24]

y-m-40-10.thinking.2: Show double count with example and correct it
y-m-40-10.prereq.1: Know combination nCr and product rule. Complement method for “at least one” may be known, but task also allows students without it.
y-m-40-10.s.s1.prompt: Before reading solution, what best first check for whether 336 possible? [336]
y-m-40-10.s.s1.hint.0: Find total possible cases before adding condition.
y-m-40-10.s.s1.hint.1: With small example, check whether adding condition increases or decreases cases. [2 4]
y-m-40-10.s.s1.o.a: Since a girl required, bigger answer is safer.
y-m-40-10.s.s1.r.a: This misses adding condition only reduces or keeps cases, never increases.
y-m-40-10.s.s1.o.b: Compare 336 with all ways to choose 4 of 10. [336 4 10]
y-m-40-10.s.s1.r.b: Conditioned cases cannot outnumber all cases.
y-m-40-10.s.s1.o.c: First find 6C4, cases choosing boys only. [6 4]
y-m-40-10.s.s1.r.c: This can find answer but is different from checking Daeun.
y-m-40-10.s.s1.o.d: First check whether answer multiple of 4, committee size. [4]
y-m-40-10.s.s1.r.d: No relation between member count and number of ways.
y-m-40-10.s.s1.explain: All choices: 10C4=210. Requiring at least 1 girl can only reduce or preserve count, never increase, so 336 impossible. This size check shows some committee counted repeatedly. [4 10 10 4 210 1 336]
y-m-40-10.s.s1.acc.0: Correct answer can be found: 210 total minus 15 all-boy choices. But this step asks if 336 is possible; comparing with 210 is more direct. [15 210 336 210]
y-m-40-10.s.s2.prompt: Choose first wrong line in Daeun solution.
y-m-40-10.s.s2.hint.0: Fix a committee with girls 가, 나 and two boys; list people who could be chosen first on line 1. [1]
y-m-40-10.s.s2.hint.1: Check if each line yields each committee exactly once.
y-m-40-10.s.s2.line.3: Thus 336 committees include at least one girl. [336 1]
y-m-40-10.s.s2.explain: Line 3 first wrong. Lines 1,2 counts 4 and 84 correct, but multiplying distinguishes first chosen girl and repeats same committee. For example committee with girls 가,나 and two boys counted twice: 가 first or 나 first. Line 4 uses line 3 value. If chose line 1 or 2, check whether count fits its sentence. [3 1 2 4 84 4 3 1 2]
y-m-40-10.s.s3.prompt: Give committee example counted repeatedly, explain 336 too high, and find correct count by one method. [336]
y-m-40-10.s.s3.hint.0: Fix committee with 2+ girls and list who could be first choice on line 1. [2 1]
y-m-40-10.s.s3.hint.1: Another way compare no-girl cases with total. Find that value.
y-m-40-10.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Girls 가 and 나 and ...
y-m-40-10.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you give concrete committee with 2+ girls and show repeat count? [2]
y-m-40-10.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you write how to get correct value (subtract total or add by girl count)?
y-m-40-10.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Did you check answer below total 210? [210]
y-m-40-10.s.s3.model.0: Committee with girls 가,나 and two boys counted twice, depending on first chosen girl. Subtract 15 with no girls from 210 total: 195. [15 210 195]
y-m-40-10.s.s3.model.1: Committees with 2+ girls repeated depending on first chosen girl, making 336. Count by 1,2,3,4 girls: 80+90+24+1=195. [2 336 1 2 3 4 80 90 24 1 195]
